- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing gradual mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices during sustained downward trends, particularly when true values are below 70.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 76+ to 78+) are common, followed by overcorrection.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 70–75 range, underestimating when true values dip below 70.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Model fails to capture short-term volatility in the 65–75 range, leading to flat or overly smooth curves.
- When history includes multiple peaks, model tends to overfit the last peak and underpredict subsequent troughs.
